T_how.T1: I estimated typical human moral-rating patterns for each phrase. Because of the half-way bias, I pushed the medians further toward the scale ends and toward Chinese views on authority and the nation. I also added a lot of spread between people.
T_how.T2: I estimated typical bilingual (mostly Chinese) raters' moral judgments per action, with clear harms near 1-2, prosocial or patriotic acts near 6-7, ambiguous acts near 4. I widened the tails to allow for disagreement and pushed medians toward likely human extremity.
T_how.T3: Estimated typical bilingual Chinese-English norms for moral valence of verb-object phrases, then compressed the extremes and widened the spreads toward the scale midpoint to allow for the noise and moderation seen in real group ratings, per the half-shift note.
T_how.T4: I began from my own sense of each action's valence. Then I shrank the medians toward the scale midpoint more than felt natural, about double my instinct, to correct for the half-way bias. I widened the tails to match typical human variability on 7-point scales.
T_how.T5: I started from the typical moral valence of each phrase. Then I pulled the medians toward the 4 midpoint, because group norms are usually more moderate than my own ratings. I widened the tails to reflect variation between raters.
T_how.T6: I judged each action's typical moral rating for bilingual (likely Chinese) adults, then pulled the medians toward the scale midpoint and widened the spreads to correct for my known overconfidence. I added a little extra weight to obedience and patriotism items.
